Wrong: an equation is just a sum to calculate. Right: it is a statement of balance between two expressions, with an unknown to find
Wrong: you may add a number to just one side. Right: whatever is done to one side must be done to the other side
Wrong: when a term moves to the other side its sign stays the same. Right: its additive inverse appears on the other side (+7 becomes -7)
Wrong: the answer of the equation is always the final answer of the story. Right: read what the question asks: the equation may give only the total, not the friends or the part
Wrong: every equation has exactly one solution. Right: an equation like 'a number plus 4 equals the number plus 5' has no solution
Wrong: a solution that looks neat must be right. Right: only substituting back proves it
